bull_bear.body:
- Uniquely positioned as the only global manufacturer offering mineral, natural ester and synthetic ester-based transformer fluids, enabling it to address utility, industrial and infrastructure applications (MD&A, Transformer Fluids)
- Among the top two suppliers of White & Mineral Oils in India (Corporate Overview product portfolio)
- First Indian lubricant company to manufacture ester molecules; synthetic ester manufacturing capability is being extended to transformer fluids, EV battery cooling and immersion cooling for data centres
- Long-standing relationships with leading automotive OEMs, with several partnerships spanning more than two decades
- Multi-brand portfolio built over decades - TRANSOL, bioTRANSOL, TRANSOL Synth, TECHNOL, SAVONOL, SAVOGEL, SAVSOL, SAVOFIL, SAVOFLOD, VITAGEL
- Export reach across over 75 countries, contributing 17% of total turnover
- Debt-free balance sheet and strong cash reserves (Chairman & Managing Director's message)
- Captive renewable energy since 1999 - 53.10 MW installed wind capacity and 2061 KWp rooftop solar, with more than 30% of total power consumed at the four manufacturing plants coming from captive solar generation at the respective plant sites
bull_bear.title: Bull — competitive strengths

bull_bear.body:
- Crude oil, base oil and feedstock price volatility — The lubricants industry remains exposed to fluctuations in crude oil and base oil prices and competitive pricing pressures; the white mineral oils business is likewise exposed to fluctuations in feedstock costs. As a specialty petroleum manufacturer the Company's procurement cost and margin move with these inputs.
- Vehicle electrification and longer lubricant drain intervals — Management states that increasing vehicle electrification and lubricant drain intervals may gradually influence lubricant demand across certain segments, even though ICE vehicles still dominate India's automotive base and EV registrations rose around 80% in FY 2025-26.
- Long qualification and approval cycles for new fluid technologies — Ester-based transformer fluids carry higher costs than conventional mineral oils and face extended qualification cycles and evolving technical standards; for new-age fluids (EV cooling, immersion cooling) commercial adoption remains dependent on technology validation, customer qualification cycles and evolving industry standards - so revenue from the ester pivot is gated by customer approval timelines.
- Regulatory and quality-standard tightening in regulated end-uses — White mineral oils face evolving regulatory requirements and increasingly stringent quality standards across pharmaceutical, personal care and food-related applications; maintaining consistent product quality and compliance with global standards is stated to be critical for sustained growth.
- Competitive intensity, import pressure and ingredient substitution — In white mineral oils, competitive intensity, import pressures and shifts towards alternative ingredients in select formulations may influence market dynamics; in lubricants, competitive pricing pressure is explicitly flagged.
- Raw material availability and changing regulation for ester fluids — Changes in raw material availability and regulatory requirements may influence adoption trends of ester-based transformer fluids across certain applications.
- Emission and efficiency regulation reshaping product requirements — BS-VI emission standards and CAFE norms continue to reshape lubricant requirements, driving a shift to low-viscosity, synthetic and semi-synthetic grades - a reformulation and requalification burden as well as a premiumisation opportunity.
- Process, fire and occupational safety at manufacturing plants — Handling of petroleum products requires an ISO 45001:2018-based OH&S management system, HIRA, permit-to-work, LOTO and extensive fire infrastructure (hydrant systems on dedicated 100 KL, 225 KL and 650 KL water storage tanks at 7 kg/cm2). Zero LTIFR, zero recordable injuries and zero fatalities were reported for employees and workers in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25.

business.body: The Company's main activity is manufacturing of coke and refined petroleum products, which accounts for 99.22% of turnover (BRSR Section A; Petroleum Products, NIC code 19201). Its portfolio spans transformer oils marketed under TRANSOL, bioTRANSOL and TRANSOL Synth; white and mineral oils and petroleum jellies under TECHNOL, SAVONOL and SAVOGEL; automotive and industrial lubricants under SAVSOL; and formulated specialty waxes, emulsions and cable compounds under SAVOFIL, SAVOFLOD and VITAGEL - sold to transformer manufacturers, power plant operators and electricity boards, to pharmaceutical, personal care, plastics and polymer customers, to automotive OEMs, and to retail customers through the B2C SAVSOL range. Operations comprise 4 plants and 5 offices, all in India, serving 25 states and union territories with exports to over 75 countries contributing 17% of turnover; the Company also operates wind power plants in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu.

- **Automotive Oils (B2B, OEM):** OEM automotive lubricants
- **Automotive Oils (B2C, retail):** SAVSOL, SAVSOL Ester5, lubricants, fluids, greases and coolants compliant with BS VI emission standards
- **Industrial Oils:** SAVSOL industrial lubricants, Hydraulic Oils, Turbine Oils, Thermic Fluids, Heavy Duty Industrial Gear Oils, Transmission Oils, Greases, Heat Treatment (Quenching) Oils, Metal Working Oils
- **Formulated & Specialty Products:** SAVOFIL, SAVOFLOD, VITAGEL, paraffin wax emulsions, microcrystalline wax, polyethylene wax, oxidised PE wax, cable filling and flooding compounds

outlook.body:
- Strengthen the SAVSOL brand and expand the B2C (retail lubricants) business
- Drive double-digit growth across domestic and international markets
- Build new growth engines around ester-based and advanced fluid technologies, leveraging the proprietary ester molecule platform
- Advance commercialisation of synthetic ester technologies across the product portfolio - transformer fluids, EV battery cooling, immersion cooling for data centres and other specialised industrial applications
- Deepen presence in high-growth transformer-fluid applications where safety, sustainability and performance drive customer decisions
- Expand adoption of ester-based transformer fluids through innovation, technical collaboration and customer engagement, backed by synthetic ester manufacturing capability
- Expand the portfolio of high-purity specialty white-oil products and deepen relationships across pharmaceutical, personal care, food-grade and industrial segments, in both domestic and international markets
- Premiumisation in lubricants - the SAVSOL Ester5 range recorded sales growth at nearly five times the industry growth rate
- Expand the distribution footprint, strengthen brand visibility and deepen customer engagement across domestic and international markets
- Strengthen R&D capabilities as the first Indian lubricant company to manufacture ester molecules
- Occupational Health & Safety Management System certified to ISO 45001:2018 covering all permanent employees and contract workers, applicable across all plants
- Integrated Quality, Environment, Health & Safety (QEHS) policy with a stated objective of maintaining zero Lost Time Injury (LTI) and proactive identification and mitigation of EHS risks for all personnel
- Management systems strengthened through certification audits for ISO 14001:2015 and ISO 45001:2018 by accredited certification bodies; 100% of plants and offices assessed for health and safety practices (ISO 45001:2018 audit by certification body Pyramid)
- Zero LTIFR, zero total recordable work-related injuries, zero fatalities and zero high-consequence injuries for both employees and workers in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25
- Transition from diesel-powered forklifts to electric forklifts to reduce emissions
- Installed a solar power system with a capacity of 500 kW at the Silli plant
- Plantation of trees within all plant premises as part of green cover enhancement
- Structured Hazard Identification and Risk Assessment (HIRA), Permit-to-Work, Management of Change and Lockout-Tagout systems, with periodic review after process, equipment, personnel or legal changes and after incidents/near-misses
- Zero complaints on Working Conditions and on Health & Safety filed by employees and workers in FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25
outlook.title: Strategy & capital allocation

outlook.body: The bundle contains no manufacturing-capacity expansion project, commissioning date or ramp-up plan. Operationally, the Directors' Report records that the Company's Wind Power Plants in Maharashtra, Karnataka and Tamil Nadu generated 94.91 MU in FY 2025-2026 against 84.26 MU in the previous year, and that during the year under review the Company did NOT add any new projects to its Wind Portfolio. Renewable and energy-efficiency investment continues at the four existing manufacturing facilities: installed renewable energy capacity of 53.1 MW, rooftop solar of 2,061 kWp installed across the 4 manufacturing facilities, plus energy-efficiency work (expansion of rooftop solar systems, replacement of diesel forklifts with battery-operated electric forklifts, LED lighting, thermic-fluid heating optimisation, insulation upgrades, thermopac overhaul, electric drum heating, energy-efficient pumps, motors and compressors and improved steam distribution), with stated reductions of 9.42% in power consumption at the Turbhe plant, 29.5% in diesel consumption at the Silvassa plant, 1,612 litres of diesel saved at the Kharadpada plant and 8-10% lower LDO consumption at the Mahad plant. Three of the four manufacturing facilities operate as Zero Liquid Discharge units and the fourth is connected to a Common Effluent Treatment Plant. On structure, the Board on 7th May, 2026 approved a Scheme of Amalgamation between Savita GreenTec Limited (Transferor) and Savita Oil Technologies Limited (Transferee) under Sections 230 to 232 of the Companies Act, 2013, subject to necessary statutory and regulatory approvals. The BRSR reports that capex investments in specific technologies to improve environmental and social impacts were Nil in both FY 2025-26 and FY 2024-25 (R&D on such technologies was 1.04% of total R&D, directed at technologically advanced ester-based products for lubricant, compressor and electric vehicle applications).
outlook.title: Capex & expansion plans

outlook.body:
- Transformer fluids: sustained investment in electricity infrastructure, renewable energy integration and grid modernisation - the global transformer oil market was valued at approximately USD 2.9 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 7.5 billion, growing at a CAGR of over 12% through 2033, with utilities the key demand driver
- India transformer demand: expansion of transmission corridors, modernisation of distribution networks and renewable energy evacuation are expected to create sustained demand for transformers and insulating fluids
- Customer shift from conventional insulating fluids to advanced fluids offering enhanced fire safety and environmental performance, visible in renewable projects, transportation systems, data centres, industrial facilities and urban utility networks
- Ester fluids: the global ester-based transformer oil market was valued at approximately USD 624.83 million in 2025 and is advancing at a 7.73% CAGR from 2026 to 2032; in India, renewable energy, transmission infrastructure, metro rail, airports, data centres and battery energy storage systems (BESS) support adoption
- White mineral oils: the global white oil market is expected to reach USD 3,386.3 million by 2033; India's domestic pharmaceutical market, valued at approximately USD 60 billion, is projected to reach USD 130 billion by 2030, reinforcing demand for high-purity ingredients
- Lubricants: the Indian lubricants market was valued at approximately USD 4.92 billion in 2025 and is projected to reach USD 7.53 billion by 2034, with automotive applications accounting for nearly 46% of total lubricant demand during the year
- Premiumisation: India's synthetic lubricants market generated revenue of approximately USD 1.02 billion in 2025 and is projected to earn revenue of USD 1,379.1 million by 2033; BS-VI and CAFE norms drive adoption of low-viscosity, synthetic and semi-synthetic lubricants
- Electrification: EV registrations increased by around 80% in FY 2025-26 and CNG adoption rose steadily - conventional lubricants still dominate, but the transition creates opportunity for specialised fluids and thermal management solutions
- Input costs: fluctuations in crude oil and base oil prices and key raw materials exerted pressure on procurement costs and margins, particularly for imported feedstocks
- Domestic capex cycle: Union Budget 2026-27 increased capital expenditure to a record `12.2 lakh crore, up from `11.2 lakh crore, with allocations to roads, railways, ports, airports, power transmission and urban infrastructure
- Growth during FY 2025-26 was broad-based - Transformer Oils, White Oils and Exports recorded double-digit growth while the Lubricants business delivered high single-digit growth
